AC6 MET — live evidence from run 31587452003 (2026-08-12, head b13173bb7d, DC harness job 94084484969).

Harness result: 1 failed, 59 passed, 1 xfailed, 1 error in 2471.11s (0:41:11) — improved from the 3 failed of run 31362329118 that opened this ticket.

Both of this ticket's cells PASSED. Verified by absence: grepping the job log for FAILED/ERROR lines naming test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing or test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance returns nothing, and the two residuals are named explicitly as other cells. So the assertions now read the canonical sync route correctly against real Jira DC, which is the only place that could be proven.

The two residuals are a DIFFERENT failure class and are not this defect:

1. ERROR tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_unassign_round_trips — CalledProcessError: ['git','fetch','origin','tickets'] exit 128, raised at setup of the dc_store_copy_repo fixture (_dc_fixtures.py:139). Filed as ancient-domestic-orca (00c6-e96e-3f04-434d) and linked discovered_from this ticket. Worth noting for whoever picks it up: that call is subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, check=True), so git's stderr is captured and then dropped by CalledProcessError, whose message carries only the exit status. The cause of the 128 therefore CANNOT be determined from this run's log — fixing the diagnostic is a prerequisite for choosing the right retry policy, which is how that ticket is written.

2. FAILED test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers — 'rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s'. Tracker write-lock contention, already covered by royal-weariless-zebrafish (10c3-5a33-2e25-4584); change 1657 in review adds retries to that write path. Not duplicated.

The 0-failed re-green bar is therefore NOT met, and I am not claiming it. AC6 has been amended in the description to say so explicitly rather than quietly narrowed: this ticket's defect is proven fixed live, and the residuals belong to their own tickets. Two live-LLM suite jobs (anthropic/openai) also failed in the same run; unrelated to this change and being triaged separately.

Closing --class preexisting: the OK:-line divergence was introduced by c87afedba8 on 2026-08-08 and lay dormant until the first live exercise of that change.
